title: Director of Optimization Engineering
description:
Opportunity

Adapture Renewables, Inc. is on a mission to be a leader in this new era of sustainable energy. Drawing upon an extensive knowledge base, we develop, finance, engineer, build, own, and operate high quality utility-scale photovoltaic projects and battery energy storage projects. Our Engineering team is looking for a talented Director of Optimization Engineering to help support the efforts of our fast-growing company. Adapture Renewables is owned by KIRKBI – the private holding and investment company of the Kirk Kristiansen family founded to build a sustainable future for the LEGO® brand through generations.

Overview

This position will work in our Engineering team and report to the Sr. Director of Engineering. The Director of Optimization Engineering owns the technical strategy for optimizing our hybrid and collocated utility-scale solar and battery energy storage (BESS) systems — driving energy production, capture, storage efficiency, and load-matching across Adapture Renewable’s multi-GW development pipeline. This is a builder’s seat: the role sets the optimization vision, defines success criteria, and grows a team of engineers to execute against it, partnering closely with Development, Interconnection & Transmission, Asset Management, and Power Marketing. The candidate will ideally be based in the San Francisco Bay Area (hybrid); remote considered for exceptional candidates.

Core Responsibilities

  • Own the engineering roadmap for hybrid solar-plus-storage optimization — from system sizing and configuration through dispatch strategy — and define the KPIs and initiatives that connect design choices to energy yield and financial return.
  • Govern PV performance modeling standards (PVSyst), including P50/P90 production estimates, degradation profiles, and loss/availability frameworks.
  • Model and optimize combined PV and BESS output to serve large-load customers such as data centers, through both front-of-meter and co-located behind-the-meter designs.
  • Set the engineering basis for battery dispatch and energy-arbitrage strategy using linear-programming methods, in coordination with Power Marketing.
  • Establish standards for solar/BESS sizing, EMS configuration, DC/AC ratios, ground coverage ratios, state-of-charge limits, and round-trip efficiency.
  • Ensure designs meet utility and interconnection requirements and SCADA/EMS protocols; partner with Interconnection & Transmission and IT on the underlying data path.
  • Direct root-cause analysis of operating-fleet underperformance (soiling, availability, equipment faults, clipping, degradation, capacity fade) and feed findings back into design and procurement.
  • Hire, develop, and lead the optimization engineering team, including the Manager of Optimization Engineering.
  • Deliver design and performance recommendations to Engineering leadership and, as needed, to ownership.

Qualifications and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in electrical, mechanical, energy, or systems engineering, or an equivalent quantitative discipline; advanced degree a plus.
  • 8+ years in renewable energy, with hands-on experience designing and optimizing utility-scale solar and demonstrated BESS experience (sizing, dispatch optimization, degradation, or performance modeling).
  • 3+ years leading and developing technical teams, with a track record of setting vision and delivering results.
  • Deep fluency in PV performance modeling (PVSyst or equivalent), including P50/P90 yield estimation and loss/availability analysis.
  • Strong PV and BESS electrical engineering foundation: inverters and DC/AC conversion, EMS configuration, state-of-charge limits, and round-trip efficiency.
  • Working command of dispatch/arbitrage optimization (linear programming or comparable methods) and the data analytics behind battery control strategies.
  • Proven ability to translate models and data into prioritized, economically grounded recommendations for engineers, executives, and owners.
  • Preferred: Python (SciPy or similar solvers), MATLAB, and SQL; SCADA/EMS and OT data architecture experience; familiarity with BESS warranty and capacity-guarantee structures; working knowledge of interconnection and market context (PPA structures, curtailment, ancillary services); PE license a plus.
  • Ability to travel occasionally to project sites and the Bay Area office.

Benefits Package

  • 401(k) plan with company matching contribution
  • Competitive health, vision, and dental benefits
  • Attractive personal time off and company holiday package
  • Work-from-home policy
  • Salary commensurate with experience, range $200,000 - $245,000

Note

Qualified candidates only. No search firms. Adapture Renewables, Inc. is committed to equal employment opportunity.

title: Office Manager
description:
Opportunity

Adapture Renewables, Inc. is an expert in developing, financing, engineering, building, and operating utility-scale photovoltaic systems and battery energy storage systems. Drawing upon an extensive knowledge base, we realize projects with speed, flexibility, and high quality. Our team is looking for an Office Manager to support our team and manage the daily operations of our Oakland, California office. This role is based in our Oakland office; the role requires two to three days per week onsite, flexing to the needs of the team and office. Adapture Renewables, Inc. is owned by KIRKBI Climate – the private holding and investment company of the Kirk Kristiansen family founded to build a sustainable future for the LEGO® brand through generations.

Overview

The Office Manager is a trusted team member and the owner of the Oakland office experience. This role will manage the office’s facilities, vendors, events, and administrative operations, while also providing some high-level executive support to the. It is a standalone role with no direct reports.

Core Responsibilities

  • Serves as a professional point of contact for internal and external executive stakeholders, exercising sound judgment on prioritization and access to leadership.
  • Owns the overall organization, cleanliness, safety, and professional appearance of the Oakland office.
  • Serves as the primary liaison with building management and manages relationships with external vendors and service providers (janitorial, catering, supplies, and equipment), including sourcing, negotiating, and tracking service agreements.
  • Manages office supplies, equipment, and furniture, and owns the office operating budget and related expenses.
  • Oversees front-of-house operations, welcoming visitors in a professional manner and managing incoming and outgoing mail and packages.
  • Plans and executes company events and employee-experience initiatives, including team-building activities, holiday parties, company meals, and celebrations.
  • Coordinates leadership and all-hands meetings end to end, including scheduling, agendas, materials, room setup, and follow-up on action items.
  • Supports new-hire onsite logistics and office onboarding, and develops, documents, and improves office policies and procedures.
  • Provides executive administrative support through complex calendar management, travel coordination, expense reporting, and preparation of confidential leadership and board materials.
  • May occasionally need to lift items weighing up to 25 lbs.
  • Working onsite in the Oakland office two to three days per week is a required, essential duty of the position.

Qualifications and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree preferred, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant work experience.
  • 3–5 years of experience supporting executives, ideally in a fast-paced corporate environment, including office management responsibility.
  • Proven ability to manage complex calendars, travel, and competing executive priorities with minimal direction.
  • Experience managing vendors, facilities, and an office operating budget.
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft 365 (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Teams)
  • Exceptional organization and attention to detail, with the ability to prioritize and meet deadlines under pressure.
  • Sound judgment, professionalism, and discretion when handling confidential and sensitive information.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.

Benefits Package

  • 401(k) plan with company matching
  • Competitive health, vision, and dental benefits
  • Attractive personal time off and company holiday package
  • Target base salary range of $80,000–$90,000 per year, depending on experience and qualifications

title: Project Manager
description:
Opportunity

Adapture Renewables, Inc. is on a mission to be a leader in this new era of sustainable energy. Drawing upon an extensive knowledge base, we develop, finance, engineer, build, own, and operate high quality utility-scale photovoltaic projects and battery energy storage projects. Our Construction team is looking for a talented Project Manager to help support the efforts of our fast-growing company. Adapture Renewables is owned by KIRKBI Climate – the private holding and investment company of the Kirk Kristiansen family founded to build a sustainable future for the LEGO® brand through generations.

Overview

This position will work in our Construction team and lead the end-to-end delivery of utility-scale solar PV and battery energy storage projects, from development and preconstruction handoff through commercial operation, owning project plans, budgets, schedules, and EPC execution while leading a project team of APMs, CMs, and Quality Managers. This position reports to the Director of Construction. The candidate may be based remotely in the U.S., with periodic travel to our Bay Area home office and other company locations.

Core Responsibilities

  • Lead and manage internal and external resources to execute through development and precon handoff to project team
  • Lead contract negotiations with EPCs and drive contract execution process
  • Lead project procurement coordination activities (e.g., modules, MPT, HV breakers)
  • Assist the development team by providing site risk assessment and mitigation options
  • Analyze site for key constructability factors based on constraint data including, but not limited to, environmental risks, easements, wetlands, and pipelines
  • Interview, hire, lead, and retain APMs, CMs, and Quality Managers to manage projects from inception to O&M
  • Manage project plans and budgets; compile revenue and cash flow forecasts; compile financial reports for executive management and shareholders
  • Manage utility requirements and GIA, including substation, switchyard, and T-line construction
  • Manage and build BESS projects, including standalone, co-located, and combined configurations
  • Drive project schedule to meet contractual EPC milestones, Utility/GIA milestones, ISO COD, and PPA COD deadlines
  • Provide support to the precon team on RFP bid reviews and technical documentation, including support in the EPC selection process
  • Conduct monthly owner site visits and assessments to monitor and manage construction EPCs
  • Implement, monitor, and improve the following systems on a project-by-project basis:
    • Site-specific safety program and site safety audits
    • Quality management program and QA/QC inspections
    • Cost management system
    • Schedule management system
  • Lead and coordinate communications with landowners, utilities, and offtakers as needed during construction
  • Report on project health regularly to management
  • Represent the construction department in relevant development and delivery meetings as required
  • Represent the construction department during relevant third-party stakeholder meetings and events as required
  • Coordinate weekly one-on-one meetings with the project team

Qualifications and Experience

  • Demonstrated experience managing utility-scale solar PV and BESS construction projects from inception through commercial operation
  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, construction management, or a related field, or equivalent industry experience
  • PVsyst energy modeling software experience
  • Experience with PV utility-scale design, including layouts and single-line diagrams
  • Experience with civil design requirements for the development of PV utility-scale projects, including site access, site drainage, and hydrology
  • Experience with various PV technologies used in utility-scale projects in the U.S. market
  • Experience with resource analysis and performance metrics and KPIs, including leading training and certification processes
  • OSHA 30 certification; CPR/First-Aid/AED; SWPPP and erosion control
  • Strong leadership, negotiation, and stakeholder communication skills
  • Position requires regular travel to project sites and other company locations

Benefits Package

  • 401(k) plan with company matching contribution
  • Competitive health, vision, and dental benefits
  • Attractive personal time off and company holiday package
  • Work-from-home policy
  • Salary commensurate with experience
  • $135,000 - $155,000, DOE

Note

Qualified candidates only. No search firms. Adapture Renewables, Inc. is committed to equal employment opportunity.

title: SCADA Engineer
description:
Opportunity

Adapture Renewables, Inc. is on a mission to be a leader in this new era of sustainable energy. Drawing upon an extensive knowledge base, we develop, finance, engineer, build, own, and operate high quality utility-scale photovoltaic projects and battery energy storage projects. Our Technology team is looking for a talented SCADA Engineer to help support the efforts of our fast-growing company. Adapture Renewables is owned by KIRKBI Climate– the private holding and investment company of the Kirk Kristiansen family founded to build a sustainable future for the LEGO® brand through generations.

Overview

This position will work in our Technology team to provide design, proactive, and reactive support services for our EPC and Asset Management teams. The SCADA Engineer will ensure that devices remain in compliance with Technology policies and procedures. The SCADA Engineer will play a key role in deploying and troubleshooting all solar power plant automation.   • Experience with inverter-based resources
  • Experience troubleshooting and programming/scripting with these languages (Bash, Python, IEC 61131-3)
  • Experience troubleshooting computer networking (TCP/IP, RS232/485, Routing/Switching, and Wireless)
  • Experience with NERC-CIP
  • Be able to travel on an as-needed basis
  • Excellent written and verbal skills are required

Benefits Package

  • 401(k) plan with company matching contribution

Salary starting at $135,000, annually, DOE.

title: Sr. Transmission Manager
description:
Opportunity

Adapture Renewables, Inc. is on a mission to be a leader in the new era of sustainable energy. Drawing upon an extensive knowledge base, we develop, engineer, and build renewable energy projects. The Interconnection and Transmission team is looking for a talented Senior Manager to help support the efforts of our fast-growing company. Adapture Renewables is owned by KIRKBI – the private holding and investment company of the Kirk Kristiansen family founded to build a sustainable future for the LEGO® brand through generations.

Overview

This position will work in our Interconnection and Transmission department to provide business development, interconnection insights, strategic system analysis and modeling support for the interconnection of utility-scale projects within designated regions of North America. This role is focused on identifying optimal strategies for interconnecting projects to the electric grid based on curtailment profile, interconnection costs, system impact assessments, real-time energy pricing, and market delivery options. In addition, the ideal candidate will support the engineering team in minimizing cost to interconnection utility scale projects. This position will report directly to the VP, Interconnection and Transmission. The candidate may be based remotely in the U.S., with periodic travel to our Bay Area home office and other company locations.

Core Responsibilities

  • Analyze optimal locations on the grid to interconnect through customary quantitative modeling (ex. SCED, power flow, etc.) as well as qualitative research.
  • Define Interconnection strategies for each market, with a clear and concise timeline to achieve successful interconnection.
  • Develop key relationships with utilities and market stakeholders.
  • Perform transmission assessments to determine commercial viability of potential projects and estimate costs of required transmission system upgrades.
  • Support and lead project due diligence efforts, identify existing and potential red flags for project acquisitions and existing pipeline projects.
  • Communicate project’s interconnection requirements, risks and opportunities to Project Development lead; support pipeline and risk reviews to assess project viability.
  • Evaluate high-level cost and schedule for various grid interconnection options and provide recommendations for optimized solutions.
  • Prepare and submit interconnection applications for Solar PV, PV + Battery and standalone battery storage projects.

Qualifications and Experience

  • BS Electrical Engineering. - Master’s Degree in Power Systems is preferred.
  • 7-10 years of engineering background with 5 years’ in utility scale electrical power systems. 3+ year of experience in grid interconnection integration of power producer resources in transmission level systems.
  • Understanding of the relationship between transmission planning and grid operations (e.g., the interplay between reliability and price formation).
  • Experience with PSS/E, MUST, TARA, PowerWorld or similar power flow software required.
  • Production costs and market simulation software (PROMOD, UPlan, Gridview, Aurora/Plexos etc.) experience a plus.
  • Experience modeling and simulating GIA upgrade costs is a strong plus.
  • Self-motivated with a high level of initiative and accountability.
  • Strong background in interconnection facility, high voltage substation, and transmission line design considerations.
  • Experience with transmission and distribution interconnection tariffs with a focus on interconnection procedures, studies, and planning process.
  • Track record of developing, communicating, and implementing innovative solutions and strategies.
  • Provide guidance on the technical aspects of grid interconnection for renewable power plants for the following project phases: development, design, construction, commissioning up to the commercial operation.
  • Strong computer skills (MS Excel, Word, Power Point).

Benefits Package

  • 401(k) plan with company matching
  • Competitive health, vision, and dental benefits
  • Attractive personal time off and company holiday package
  • Work-from-home policy
  • Salary commensurate with experience, range from $180,000 - 210,000.
